standard_prerequisites: The diagonal function diag mapping the Godel number of a formula with one free variable to the Godel number of its diagonalization, and its representing formula D_diag in Q, with the two representability facts established at the start of the unit's fixed-point section: Q derives the instance relating the diagonalization input to the output, and Q derives the universal statement forcing any witnessed y to equal the Godel number of the diagonalization.
core_obligations: Given B(x), form E(x) as the existential formula saying that some y diagonalizes x and satisfies B(y), and let A be the diagonalization of E.

Prove the left-to-right direction: assuming A, unpack E, use the uniqueness fact from the representing formula to force the witnessed y to be the Godel number of A, and conclude B of that Godel number.
Prove the right-to-left direction: assuming B of the Godel number of A, combine with the representation instance for the pair to witness the existential, which is exactly A.
proof_roadmap: Define E and A, then derive the two representability facts for the specific pair of Godel numbers appearing in the argument.
Both directions of the biconditional are short existential manipulations; the only care point is using the uniqueness fact to pin the witnessed y.
difficulty_reason: A self-reference construction with a two-direction biconditional; the substantive step is the diagonalization setup plus the uniqueness pinning of the witnessed y, each direction remaining a short first-order manipulation.
